correctness.rationale: For 0<c<v the contributor set is exactly a maximal independent set. On a cycle binary gap lengths must be 2 or 3; two selected chord endpoints remove c_d c_(n-d) previously valid equilibria, while one new neighbor rescues exactly 2 c_(d-2)c_(n-d-2) otherwise undominated profiles. The difference D(d,m)=c_(d+m-3)-c_d c_m+2c_(d-2)c_(m-2) obeys D(d,m)=D(d,m-2)+D(d,m-3); nonnegative base sequences for m=2,3,4 and d=2,3,4 force D>=0 with equality iff d=3 or m=3, including n=5. The difference for d=2 is c_(n-4)-c_(n-5), nonnegative with exactly the stated finite equalities. Dominant plastic-root asymptotics establish minimum/P_n ->1-1/(2alpha+3). Independently enumerated all contributor profiles for 65 n,chord combinations, n=5..14 (not substituted for all-n recurrence).

value.rationale: The welfare-independent question of how one new social connection changes equilibrium multiplicity is natural in local public-goods games. Exact all-n chord optimization with a unique reflection class, sign reversal for short chords and an explicit 17.7008% asymptotic reduction is a motivated structural graph-game theorem, not a routine restatement of the Perrin cycle count.

limitations: Finite uniform binary-action pure Nash equilibria on one-chord simple cycles, n>=5, 2<=d<=n-2. No welfare/selection dynamics conclusions; finite enumeration is not the all-n proof.
residual_risks: An unindexed chorded-cycle maximal-independent-set or independent-domination polynomial may contain the entire formula.
